source.title: ProtTeX: Structure-In-Context Reasoning and Editing of Proteins with Large Language Models
source.authors: Zi-Cheng Ma; Chuanliu Fan; Zhicong Wang; Zhen-Yu Chen; Xiao-Han Lin; Yan-Heng Li; Shihao Feng; Zi-Qiang Cao; Jun Zhang; Yi-Qin Gao

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text, including supplementary sections, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares downstream protein-function task scores for 1B- and 8B-parameter models, using task metrics rather than held-out language-model loss or a power-law fit.
record.gate_note: The relevant result is the model-scale ablation in Table 4 and the accompanying statement that the 8B model slightly outperforms the 1B model. The cited scaling-law claim in the conclusion is not itself tested. Other ablation results do not test the listed claim versions.
record.test_reason: A weak, new-setting test of V6 only. The study fine-tunes a 1B and an 8B Llama-family base model on the same protein-function data (PFUD) and compares downstream task scores (Table 4, A.4). Two sizes can show the direction of the scale effect but not whether it is predictable. No loss sweeps, power-law fits or allocation experiments are reported. The scaling-law statement in the conclusion is a citation, not a result.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. In A.4 the authors say the 8B model 'slightly outperforms' the 1B model. They call the small gap 'not unexpected given the limited dataset size' and pick 8B partly for scalability. In the conclusion they cite LLM scaling laws to anticipate gains from larger models and more data, which they do not test.
record.recipe_differences: This is a two-size comparison of fine-tuned models using protein-function task metrics, not a held-out language-model cross-entropy sweep or power-law fit.
record.peer_reviewed: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
record.problems: The scaling comparison covers only 1B and 8B models on the PFUD task; the authors note that the dataset is limited and the performance gap is small. No uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: None of the other reported outcomes directly test the listed claim versions. In particular, the other Table 4 ablations compare training data or strategy rather than model scale.

untested.parts: Whether the improvement is predictable (a trend across more than two sizes, or a relation to pretraining loss). There is no prediction from smaller models, no loss-to-task mapping, and only one task family (PFUD protein-function QA).
No held-out loss versus parameters, tokens or compute.
No shape comparison at fixed size.
No power-law form in the protein or fine-tuning regime. A two-point comparison cannot show functional form.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's limits_scope label was dropped. 'Slight' is not a condition under which V6 fails, since V6 states no magnitude, and the narrow test (two sizes, one task) belongs under untested parts. The 1B and 8B runs may differ in base-model family or pretraining as well as size, which weakens this as a clean scale comparison. The other Table 4 rows (LoRA, PSPD pretraining, multi-task) correctly have no rows, since they vary training data or method rather than scale.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out language-model loss sweep over parameters, tokens, or compute is reported.
No power-law fit or extrapolation from smaller runs to larger runs is reported.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or compute-optimal parameter/token split is reported.
No comparison of architecture shape at fixed parameter count is reported.
No test of power-law scaling across modalities or training regimes is reported.
Only protein-function task performance for a 1B-versus-8B model comparison is tested; broader scale trends and prediction from pretraining loss are not tested.
No fitted exponents, compute-optimal split, or sensitivity to power-law fitting choices is examined.

relationships.condition: PFUD protein-function QA, full fine-tuning on PFUD only, 1B versus 8B base model, single runs
relationships.reason: The 8B model scores higher than the 1B model on all five metrics (r1–r5). The gain is small, has no uncertainty, and comes from only two sizes, so it supports direction only, not predictability.
relationships.display_finding: The 8B model scored higher on all five metrics, but small gains from two single-run sizes without uncertainty estimates established only an improvement trend.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
